case_name: Dr. Prashant Kumar vs State Of Bihar & Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Bihar, Shweta Prabhat (wife)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife alleged she was beaten up and abused after marriage; petitioners seek quashing of cognizance taken against them.

legal_principles.principle: The ambit and scope of inherent power of the High Court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. in quashing of the criminal proceeding in non-compoundable offences relating to matrimonial dispute is limited.
legal_principles.held: Recently discussed and adjudicated by a three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs. Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr. [(2013) 4 SCC 58].
cited_cases: Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs. Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr., (2013) 4 SCC 58
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in understanding the court's power to quash criminal proceedings

legal_principles.principle: The State has no objection if the criminal prosecution is set aside when parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the court.
legal_principles.held: Mr. Jharkhandi Upadhyay, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State has submitted that since the case arises out of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the court, the State has got no objection, if the criminal prosecution is set aside.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — significance in understanding the State's role in criminal proceedings

outcome.final_order: Cognizance taken by trial court set aside.
